checks.claim: Night of 22/23 April 1794: the rising began at about 00:30 with a cannon shot from the arsenal, followed by all the church bells. About 400 insurgents faced a Russian garrison of about 2,000 men with 19 guns.
checks.correction: Confirmed by two independent sources. Polish Wikipedia: 'około godziny 0:30 po wystrzale armatnim z arsenału', about 400 insurgents against 'około 2 tysięcy żołnierzy z 19 armatami'. The Sułek excerpt: '0.30 val. prie arsenalo nugriaudėjo pabūklas… suskambo visų bažnyčių varpai'. On the guns there is a discrepancy: Tuchkov says only 1.5 artillery companies with 15 guns remained in the city. His darkness quote is verified word for word: 'в трех шагах нельзя было различить даже цвета одежды'. Moon check (my own Meeus calculation): last quarter fell at 02:27 local mean time on 23 April, so the moon was about half lit and very low or not yet risen at 00:30. That fits a pitch-dark night.

checks.claim: Catholic and Orthodox Easter both fell on 20 April 1794 (Gregorian), so the rising began on the night after Easter Tuesday. The report marked this 'unverified'.
checks.correction: Upgrade from unverified. I computed it myself: Gregorian Easter 1794 = Sunday 20 April, and Julian Easter = 9 April Julian = 20 April Gregorian. Tuchkov states outright that the Greek and Roman churches kept Easter on the same day that year. 22 April was a Tuesday and 23 April a Wednesday. Russian Wikipedia on Arsenyev ('в ночь на 9 апреля, день Святой Пасхи') puts the attack on Easter night itself, which is wrong. It also says Arsenyev was held until Knorring took Vilnius on '1 сентября', another error: the city fell on 1 August Julian, which is 12 August Gregorian.

checks.claim: Arsenyev was captured at the Pac Palace, Didžioji g. 7.
checks.correction: Plausible, but only Sułek supports it, and he writes 'Paco rūmų Pilies gatvėje' ('the Pac Palace on Pilies Street'). The building at Didžioji 7 is not named in any source. Vilnius has a second Pac Palace, at Šv. Jono g. 3, but it had belonged to Chancellor Aleksander Sapieha since 1783. That makes Didžioji 7 the most likely candidate by elimination. The Lithuanian and Polish Wikipedia pages on Didžioji 7 do not mention 1794 or Arsenyev. For the art team: Didžioji 7 was rebuilt in 1839–41 after its 1831 confiscation, and again in 1860 and 1909, so today's facade is not the 1794 facade.

checks.claim: Kossakowski was seized in the 'Müller house' on Niemiecka (German) Street, today reportedly Vokiečių g. 26.
checks.correction: Only LRT (Maria Makaruk, 25 April 2024) gives 'ulica Niemiecka 374 (obecnie Vokiečių g. 26)'. Sułek confirms only 'Milerio name, Vokiečių gatvėje' ('the Müller house on Vokiečių Street'). The building now at Vokiečių g. 26 is a 3-storey block recorded as built in 1960 (kurgyvenu.lt, a building-registry aggregator). After WWII Vokiečių Street was widened several times, and historic buildings survive on one side only. So nothing can be back-dated here: the house would have to be reconstructed from old plans, and the old lot may not match today's address. Arrest date: 23 April per VLE and LRT, 24 April per Polish Wikipedia ('24 kwietnia… osadzony w Arsenale'). This conflict is still open.

checks.claim: On 25 April Kossakowski was hanged in front of the Town Hall in a yellow dressing gown. Sources conflict on the time: 'at noon' (LRT) against about 14:00. Burial conflicts between St Stephen's cemetery and the Jonava crypt.
checks.correction: The place and the gown are confirmed. Polish Wikipedia: 'powieszony w żółtym szlafroku na szubienicy przed Ratuszem' ('hanged in a yellow dressing gown on a gallows before the Town Hall'). The time conflict comes from misreading LRT. LRT says the gallows was put up on Town Hall Square at noon and the hetman was brought by carriage 'dwie godziny później' ('two hours later'). So the hanging was around 14:00, which agrees with DoRzeczy. Burial: VLE says the crypt of St James's Church in Jonava ('Jonavos Šv. apaštalo Jokūbo bažnyčios rūsyje'), and Jonava parish and municipal pages list his remains in the family crypt. LRT says he was first buried without a coffin at St Stephen's cemetery. The two can be reconciled as a first burial followed by reburial, but no source dates a transfer, so that part stays unverified. One Jonava municipal page gives the hanging as 24 April, an outlier.

checks.claim: The Town Hall tower collapsed on 19 June 1781 at about 15:30, and the building was rebuilt from 1785 to 1799, so it had no tower in 1794. 'The building was 19.52 m square.'
checks.correction: The dates are confirmed. The official Town Hall site says the renovation 'spanned from 1785 to 1799'. LNDM shows Gucevičius's facade and section drawings dated 1785–1786 and says the building was rebuilt by 1799. ldkistorija gives the collapse as 19 June 1781 at about 3.30 pm, after shoring work began on 9 June. One detail is wrong: ldkistorija gives 19.52 m as the side of the tower's base, not of the building. How far construction had got by April 1794 is still unsourced.

checks.claim: Cathedral: work stopped in 1792 for lack of money, and the rebuild was finished in 1801.
checks.correction: Confirmed. ldkistorija says reconstruction was cancelled in 1792 because of Bishop Massalski's financial crisis and completed in 1801, when M. Schultz (Šulcas) finished it. VLE gives the rebuild as 1783–1801. The report missed one thing: VLE dates the three pediment statues (St Helena, St Casimir, St Stanislaus, by K. Jelski) to 1792. They were destroyed in 1950 and today's are 1997 replicas by S. Kuzma. So a 1794 scene should show the statues on a largely finished exterior with an unfinished interior.

checks.claim: Gates of Dawn: gate built 1503–14. Wooden chapel 1668–72, burned 1711–15; brick chapel about 1713–20. The 1828–30 rebuild added the classicist street facade, the gallery and the stairs. A 1785 rule required everyone to walk bareheaded from the gate to the Pociej Chapel.
checks.correction: Gate, 1503–14: confirmed by VLE and English Wikipedia. The whole wall circuit was finished only by 1522 (sanctuary site). Chapel: the sanctuary site says wooden chapel 1671, burned 1711, stone chapel 1712–1715. VLE says wooden 1671, burned 1715. The 1829 classicist rebuild is confirmed. Correction: VLE dates the gallery to 1830 and the stairs to 1879 (architect P. de Rossi), so the stairs were not part of the 1828–30 works. The 1785 rule is confirmed by the sanctuary's own site. The same 1785 order also banned street trading during services. No reliable source was found for the claim that the chapel and icon were damaged in 1794 and repaired that year; that remains secondary.

checks.claim: The city walls were pulled down in 1799–1805 and only the Gates of Dawn survived. The Lower Castle's bricks were sold in 1799 and the ruins were largely gone by the early 1800s. The Grand Duchy's artillery arsenal worked until 1795.
checks.correction: Walls: the 1799–1805 demolition is confirmed by VLE (via search results) and English Wikipedia; most wall sections came down in 1799–1802. Palace of the Grand Dukes: 'almost completely demolished in 1801, the bricks and stones were sold', after about 150 years of abandonment. So in 1794 it stood as a large ruin next to the working arsenal. The arsenal working until 1795 is supported by Lithuanian Wikipedia and National Museum material on the Old Arsenal (Arsenalo g. 3). Which building held the insurgent HQ and the prison is still unsourced.

checks.claim: Vilnius fell on 12 August 1794, after the first assault of 19–20 July. Warsaw's Tomb of the Unknown Soldier carries 'WILNO 22 IV – 13 VIII 1794'.
checks.correction: Confirmed. VLE: '08 12 kapituliavo Vilnius' ('Vilnius capitulated on 12 August'). Polish Wikipedia: '19 lipca Rosjanie przypuścili szturm' ('on 19 July the Russians attacked') and '12 sierpnia Wilno skapitulowało' ('on 12 August Vilnius capitulated'). Kurier Wileński says the capitulation letter reached Knorring on the morning of 12 August, after which the troops entered. Col. Deev's death on 9 (20) July is confirmed by Russian Wikipedia. The Tomb inscription is confirmed by Polish Wikipedia and was added after 1990. It says 13 VIII, one day off the capitulation date, so do not use it as an event date. Moon (my calculation): full moon at 09:11 local mean time on 11 August, so the night of 11/12 August was essentially full-moon.

checks.claim: After 12 August: Repnin was appointed governor-general on 30 October 1794 and arrived on 7 December. Russian troops returned, plus a new police force with Russian officers and translators. The Magdeburg charter was abolished.
checks.correction: The Repnin dates, 30 October and 7 December 1794 (arriving from Grodno), come only from Kurier Wileński. The article does not say which calendar it uses; if the dates are Julian, they would be 10 November and 18 December Gregorian. Russian Wikipedia says only that he served in Lithuania 'с октября 1794 года' ('from October 1794'). The same Kurier article dates the police force and the abolition of Magdeburg law (replaced by Catherine II's 1785 city statute) to 1795, not autumn 1794. So an October–November 1794 setting should not include the new police. Use Russian garrison troops and the old magistrate structures instead. Confirmed from the same article: loss of capital status on 14 December 1794, and the oath of 28 December 1794 in St John's (clergy and citizens) and St Casimir's (city authorities, 71 merchants, 154 property-owning burghers and 665 craftsmen).

checks.claim: The Lithuania Governorate was formed on 12 December 1796 and split on 9 September 1801. The Third Partition treaty was signed on 24 October 1795, and Stanisław August abdicated at Grodno on 25 November 1795.
checks.correction: The governorate dates are Julian, the calendar trap the report itself warns about. Russian Wikipedia gives 12 [23] December 1796 and 9 [21] September 1801, so the Gregorian dates are 23 December 1796 and 21 September 1801. The partition dates are confirmed: 24 October 1795, and 25 November 1795 at Grodno, the anniversary of the coronation (Muzeum Historii Polski, Polish Wikisource text of the act). The report left out the final partition convention of 26 January 1797. Likely Julian date, unverified: Arsenyev's death on '1 November 1796', which would be 12 November Gregorian.

checks.claim: Since 2011 the Israel Antiquities Authority and Lithuanian heritage bodies have excavated the Great Synagogue site, co-directed by Jon Seligman. Kukliansky, Krinsky, Katz and Avidan dispute its future (Jerusalem Post, 5 August 2026).
checks.correction: Start date: work on the Shulhoyf (the synagogue courtyard) began in 2011, and the 2026 season is the sixth (Times of Israel, 4 August 2026). But the Jerusalem Post/JTA article says Seligman first proposed the dig in 2013 and the excavation began in 2015. So the joint IAA–KPIP project dates from 2015, not 2011. The partners are the IAA and Kultūros paveldo išsaugojimo pajėgos (KPIP). The JPost article is confirmed: 'Archaeologists uncover treasures of Vilnius' Great Synagogue as Lithuanian Jews dispute its future', Shira Li Bartov/JTA, 5 August 2026. It gives the four positions as the report describes: Kukliansky, community centre; Krinsky, living religious centre; Katz, rebuild or keep as a religious site; Avidan, broad cultural centre.

checks.claim: Visual reference: Smuglewicz's 20+ views of Vilnius (1785–86) are in the Vilnius University Library digital collections as 24 prints.
checks.correction: The report mixes up two collections. The 24 prints on the VU Library page are Marco Carloni's engravings after Smuglewicz of Roman subjects: 23 from 'Vestigia delle Terme di Tito' and one of Villa Madama. They are not views of Vilnius. VLE confirms a 'Vilniaus vaizdų ciklas 1785–86' ('cycle of Vilnius views'). VU Library news says about twenty Vilnius views are known, commissioned by Adam Kazimierz Czartoryski and Joachim Chreptowicz; this is from a search summary. Where the originals are held, whether they are digitized, and under what licence are all unverified; VU Library holds at least the 1786 drawing of the University's Great Courtyard. Smuglewicz lived in Warsaw from 1786 to 1797, so he was not in Vilnius in 1794.

verification.notes:
Scope. The only relayed user message was 'whatsup'. The fact-check task came from the workflow script. It is research only and does not conflict with that message, so I did it. The only file I created is a calculation script in the scratchpad (astro.py). Nothing else was written.

Other checks that passed (not among the 14 above):
- Gazeta Narodowa Wileńska ran from 4 May to 6 August 1794, on Sundays and Wednesdays (Polish Wikipedia). About 28 issues (nos. 1–28) are digitized in the Jagiellonian Digital Library (jbc.bj.uj.edu.pl). The report did not know this.
- Šiauliai act, 16 April 1794 (VLE). First known Lithuanian-language proclamation, 30 April (VLE). Wielhorski in command from 4 June (VLE).
- Act of Insurrection read on Town Hall Square on 24 April (Polish Wikipedia).
- City guard announced at the Town Hall on 1 May, led by Gucevičius (LRT). The Council's circular of 15 May was printed at the Academy press. The LMAVB (Wróblewski Library) exhibition ran until 12 September 2014.
- Poczobutt weather record (Bukantis & Stankūnavičius, EMS): observations began in 1770, the series is complete from 1777, and the thermometer was at a north window 20.6 m up. The record is a daily astronomical log ('Cahiers des observations…'), probably handwritten. Whether the 1794 pages survive is unverified.
- Tuchkov's memoir: the imwerden PDF works (23.6 MB) and so does wars175x tchk61. The 1908 edition is public domain.
- Sułek's book: 'Sprzysiężenie Jakuba Jasińskiego', Warsaw, Wydawnictwo MON, 1982, 280 pp., ISBN 83-11-06822-4. Found via bookseller and Google Books listings. This closes the report's 'unverified' note on the Polish original.
- Jewish residence ruling of 1783: Jews barred only from the Ostra Brama–Cathedral street and the Trakai Gate–St John's street. JewishGen also gives Jewish population figures (3,887 in 1765, 6,971 in 1800) and 'around thirty Jews' killed in a suburb by the incoming Russian army. JewishGen is a secondary, community-run source.
- Street lighting: oil lamps (hemp oil) appeared on main streets only at the start of the 19th century. Lamps burned until 2 a.m. and were not lit on moonlit nights.

Smaller corrections:
- Tuchkov says the 'R.Z.' letters were written in red pencil or crayon ('красным карандашом'), not chalk.
- Tuchkov's own count of the force he withdrew is 2,200 infantry, about 200 gunners and about 70 Cossacks, roughly 2,470 men. The report's 2,313 men and 11 guns does not come from Tuchkov.
- Gucevičius died on 10 December 1798 (VLE, English Wikipedia). His grave is unknown and only presumed to be at St Stephen's.
- Arsenyev's capture counts differ. Russian Wikipedia gives about 60 officers and 600 men, not 50.
- Jewish share of the population: 6,971 of about 17,000–20,000 is about 35–40%. 'Nearly half' overstates it, and the figures also cover different areas (the Jewish count includes the suburbs).

Astronomy (my own Meeus calculation, local mean time = UT + 1 h 41 min; check against a proper ephemeris):
- 23 April: last quarter at 02:27.
- 11 August: full moon at 09:11.
- 9 October: full moon at 01:58.
- New moon at 00:03 on 24 October, i.e. the night of 23/24 October, not '24–25 October'.
- Full moon again on 7 November.
- So the darkest late-autumn window is about 19–28 October. Around 30 October, when Repnin was appointed, the moon is a waxing half moon. Around 4–7 November (Praga) it is near full.
- Sunset on 25 October at about 16:40 is consistent.
- 20 July: the sun never goes 18° below the horizon, so there is no astronomical darkness. It does on 11/12 August, briefly.

Important gaps in the report, where the back-dating method fails on the spine:
1. Bishops' Palace (today's Presidential Palace). It was rebuilt in 1824–34 by Vasily Stasov in Empire style, and 'Stasov's reconstruction… has remained to this day'. Massalski's palace of 1794 has to be reconstructed; it cannot be back-dated.
2. Pac Palace, Didžioji 7. Rebuilt in 1839–41, 1860 and 1909.
3. Vokiečių Street. Widened after WWII, with historic buildings on one side only. The Müller house site now holds a building of about 1960.
4. Cathedral pediment statues. Today's are 1997 replicas of the 1792 originals, so correct in form but modern.
5. Gates of Dawn. The chapel's 1829 classicist facade, the 1830 gallery and the 1879 stairs must all be removed.
6. Town Hall. Mid-construction in 1794, state unknown.
7. Lower Castle. The palace ruin and arsenal complex must be added back; the palace was demolished in 1801.

Still open: which calendar Kurier Wileński's Repnin dates use; how far the Town Hall rebuild had got by April 1794; where the Council actually sat; which Arsenal building held the HQ and prison; the 1794 damage to the Gates of Dawn chapel; where Kossakowski was first buried; whether Kościuszko ever came to Vilnius (no evidence found); and the Wirtualny Sztetl figures (the site returned HTTP 403).

MCP servers figma and mobbin need authorization in the user's connector settings (claude.ai) or via /mcp before they can be used. They were not needed for this task.

research.summary:
A remote-only pipeline can back-date every spine building from evidence. Its core is the Lithuanian Cultural Heritage Register (KVR). It has an open bulk file (data.gov.lt dataset 2192, CC BY 4.0, 26,059 immovable objects, no addresses or coordinates). It also has a public ArcGIS REST layer (kvr.kpd.lt/arcgis/rest/services/KVR/pub_kvr_objektai) and an undocumented JSON service behind kvr.kpd.lt. For each object that service returns: dating and alteration chronology ('Century'), style, architects, 'valuable features' text (volume, storeys, roof form, facade, each with dated alteration notes), photo-survey lists and downloadable PDFs of the heritage board's evaluation acts. The acts carry house histories, archive call numbers and bibliographies. I harvested all 470 registered objects in the bbox; the data is in the scratchpad.

Counts. In the bbox 54.673–54.687 N, 25.284–25.292 E, OSM has 661 building features and the national GRPK footprint layer has 594. Measured from the spine centreline:
- within 40 m (street frontage): 106 OSM / 96 GRPK buildings
- within 60 m: 149 / 159
- within 100 m (about one block either side): 270 / 271
- within 150 m (about two blocks): 414 / 419

The KVR has 341 building-type objects in the bbox (63 / 97 / 163 / 232 in the same bands). 69 of the 110 OSM addresses on Pilies, Didžioji and Aušros Vartų match a listed building exactly; 65 of 87 match by base house number. Everything else sits inside the protected Old Town site (KVR 16073) and UNESCO site 541.

The 18th-century architectural studies are mostly offline. The Soviet-era Monument Restoration Design Institute (PRPI) studies and measured drawings are in Vilnius Regional State Archives fund 1019; its research-files inventory is being digitised in 2026. The heritage department's library holds the main dossiers and an 1808 city plan. KPEPIS, the heritage e-services system, needs a login. Remote access means ordering scans. For the Old Town proper, the public-domain historical sources go no earlier than:
- the 1737 Fürstenhoff plan
- Smuglewicz's 1785–86 views
- Jan Kunicki's 1805 Old Town plan (8137x6230 px on Commons, from the Lithuanian State Historical Archives)
- the 1912 reprint of a late-18th-century plan (Polish National Library)
- Wilczyński's Album Wileńskie (1840s onward)
- Czechowicz, Fleury and Bułhak photographs, and many pre-1939 photos on Polona

Modern geometry is free under CC BY 4.0 with National Land Service attribution (order D1-395, in force since 2025-01-01): orthophotos (the 1:2000 county-centre ortho, ≤10 cm), LiDAR (2017 county-centre set at >30 points/m², plus 2025–26 national scans) and GRPK footprints. The city's GIS company, ID Vilnius, serves 2019 and 2022 photogrammetric meshes, its own orthophotos and a 3D buildings layer with height, storeys and construction year, but the licence is unverified.

Street-level imagery is the weak point:
- Mapillary is CC BY-SA, but its API needs a token, so spine coverage is unverified.
- KartaView has no photos within 300 m.
- Google cannot be used. The consumer terms bar copying; the geo guidelines say "You may not screenshot Street View imagery"; the platform terms bar tracing building outlines from Street View and deriving 3D models from 45-degree or photorealistic 3D imagery.

Back-dating cannot be a blanket rule. The register shows top storeys added in 1718, after 1749, 1775–90, 1800, 1881 and 1889, and in the 20th century, so each building needs its own evidence.

The method follows Assassin's Creed Unity (historians on the team, 150+ old plans studied, landmarks built at 1:1, a few deliberate anachronisms) and heritage practice: London Charter paradata, the Seville Principles, and the Apollonio 7+1-level uncertainty scale. It is a 10-step per-building dossier with per-feature confidence grades A/B/C and a separate gameplay-deviation layer. Footprints to ship in the game should come from GRPK (CC BY) rather than OSM, whose ODbL licence is share-alike.

findings.claim: KVR bulk open data exists (CC BY 4.0), but it has no addresses or coordinates
findings.detail:
data.gov.lt dataset 2192 'Kultūros vertybių registro duomenys'. Publisher: Kultūros paveldo departamentas (the heritage department). Licence CC BY 4.0, updated quarterly; page says last updated 2025-12-18. Two XLSX distributions:
- /datasets/2192/distribution/13134/download/ (immovable heritage, 3.5 MB, 26,059 rows)
- 13133 (movable heritage)
Immovable fields: unikalus_kodas, priklauso_kompleksui, nr_komplekse, pavadinimas, registracijos_data, statusas, reikšmingumas, potipis, klasifikacija, value-type flags (architektūrinis, urbanistinis ...), apskritis, savivaldybė, seniūnija. There is no address, dating or coordinates, so the file alone cannot be joined to buildings. A public request for object centre coordinates was filed on the portal on 2026-09-19 (request 14527). Vilnius city has 3,249 immovable entries; the Old Town site is 'Vilniaus senamiestis', code 16073, type Vietovė, status Paminklas.

findings.claim: KVR has a public ArcGIS REST service that gives every registered object's code, name, status and address, with geometry, for spatial joins
findings.detail:
https://kvr.kpd.lt/arcgis/rest/services/KVR/ (ArcGIS 10.3) offers pub_kvr_objektai/MapServer:
- layer 0: points
- layer 1: territory polygons
Fields: ObjectId (GUID), Code (unique code), Name, NameOfficial, ObjectName, Status, Address. Native CRS is LKS-94 (EPSG:3346); queries accept inSR/outSR=4326. maxRecordCount is 1000; the internal kvr_objektai_centras layer allows 20000. Other services: pub_kvr_apsaugos_zonos (protection zones) and kvr_teritoriju_ribos (urban heritage areas).
A bbox query on 2026-09-26 returned 244 point and 226 polygon objects: 470 in total, 341 of them building-type (Paminklas 47, Valstybės saugomas 163, Registrinis 131). The service states no licence; assume the register's CC BY 4.0, which is unverified. The human-readable page for an object is https://kvr.kpd.lt/#/static-heritage-detail/{GUID}.

findings.claim: An undocumented KVR JSON service returns per-building dating, alteration chronology, protected features, act PDFs and photo surveys
findings.detail:
Base URL https://kvr.kpd.lt/KvrWcf/LabbisServiceKvr.svc, found in the public web app's kvr.js. Endpoints:
- GET /GetStaticHeritageDetails/{guid}: returns UniqueCode, Status, Address, Century (dating and alteration chronology), Style, Author (architects), ObjectCharacteristics, and ObjectFeatures (the 'valuable features' text: volume, storeys, roof form, facade solution, details, constructions). Each item carries dated alteration notes and references to IKONOGR (iconography) and FF (photo-survey) numbers.
- POST /GetStaticHeritageDocuments/{guid}: legal acts with e-tar links and Attaches[].
- GET /GetDocument/{attachId}: PDF or JPEG download.
- POST /GetStaticHeritageMedia/{guid}/2F7EEF39-03BB-4D92-B735-2FA7F3926E0B/0: photo list with Author, Date, Code, Description.
- GET /GetImage/{id}: 800 px JPEG.
- POST /GetStaticHeritagesResearchMaterial/{guid}: almost always empty (4 of 470 objects).
POST calls need 'Content-Length: 0'; the search endpoints (GetStaticHeritages) returned HTTP 500 to scripted calls.
Example, Pilies g. 19 (code 27443): 'pastatytas XVI a.; Š flygelis XIX a. I p., rekonstruotas XIX a. pab., XX a. pr., 1974 m.'; features '3 a. su rūsiais', gable roof; east facade windows changed and upper-floor openings made in the late 19th/early 20th c.; reconstruction architect Vincentas Gorskis.
Coverage within 100 m of the spine: all 163 building objects have Century and ObjectFeatures; all have photos (9,041 in total, mostly surveys from 2010–12 and 2019–23); 139 have evaluation-board acts listed; 97 have downloadable attachments. The harvested JSON is in the scratchpad (kvr_details.json, kvr_details_poly.json, kvr_rows_all.json).

findings.claim: KVR evaluation-board acts give house histories, 18th-century owners, dated storey additions and archive call numbers, but the iconography appendices are usually not online
findings.detail:
Example act KPD-RM-1586/1 (2024-11-05) for Pilies g. 19: 12-page PDF, attachment E48E8B62-0BC8-4A99-B9A3-3C0224DB0F94. The PDF text uses a font encoding shifted by 29 code points; decode it before parsing.
It records:
- the 1790 owner, Karl Friedrich Trebert of Königsberg
- that the house burned several times in the first half of the 18th c., the courtyard building was built at the end of the 18th c., and the third storey was added in the 19th c.
- the V. Gorskis reconstruction in the late 19th c. and the 1974 reconstruction
Its bibliography cites:
- Vilnius Regional State Archives (VRVA) f.1019 ap.12 b.32983 (1963 measured drawings), b.32985/32986 (1969 drawings), b.32982 (1977 facade colour project); ap.11 b.175 (1973 archaeology report)
- Lithuanian State Historical Archives (LVIA) f.544 ap.1 b.16639 (a 1909 project)
- main dossier G371K (2002) in the heritage department's library
- the 1808 and 1938 city plans in that library
- Čaplinskas, 'Pilies gatvė' (2005), pp. 230–231
- Glinska and Vitkauskienė, 'Atrastas Vilnius' (2023)
- Klovas et al. (2021)
- Paknys (2006)
The appendices ('Fotofiksacija, 52 nuotraukos'; 'Ikonografija, 34 lapai') were not in the online PDF. Whether this is typical of other acts is unverified.

findings.claim: Building counts: about 100 on the street frontage, about 270 within one block either side, about 415 within two blocks; about 60% have an individual KVR entry
findings.detail:
The bbox is roughly 1.55 x 0.51 km.
- OSM (maps.mail.ru Overpass mirror, data timestamp 2026-09-26T13:53Z): 661 building features (603 ways, 58 relations); 641 excluding garages, roofs, sheds, kiosks, bridges and construction; 445 unique addresses. Tag coverage: building:levels 125, height 124, roof:shape 187, ref:lt:kpd 17.
- GRPK national footprints (PASTAT layer): 594 in the bbox (585 of at least 20 m2).
The spine centreline was built from the OSM Pilies, Didžioji and Aušros Vartų ways plus two manual segments across Cathedral Square (about 1.6 km). Counts by distance from it:
- 40 m: 106 OSM, 96 GRPK, 63 KVR buildings
- 60 m: 149, 159, 97
- 100 m: 270, 271, 163
- 150 m: 414, 419, 232
On the three spine streets OSM has 110 addresses (Pilies 33, Didžioji 41, Aušros Vartų 36). 69 match a KVR building exactly (24, 27, 18); by base house number 65 of 87 (24/29, 27/37, 14/21). The KVR has 111 building-type objects addressed to these streets.
Caveats: KVR objects are not one-to-one with footprints (complex parts, multi-wing houses), and polygon centroids approximate positions.

findings.claim: Top storeys were added between 1718 and the 1990s, so 'remove the top storey' is not a safe default
findings.detail:
Dated additions mined from KVR texts in the bbox (32 statements, 28 objects):
- 1718, Pilies g. 17 (27440): third storey added, so 3 storeys in 1794
- after the 1749 fire, Universiteto g. 5: third storeys
- 1775–1790, Dominikonų g. 15: third storeys
- mid to late 18th c., Pilies g. 36: third storey
- late 18th to first half 19th c., Didžioji g. 15: third storey (ambiguous around 1794)
- 1800, Pilies g. 8 (650): third storey, so 2 storeys in 1794 (grade A)
- 1803, Universiteto g. 7: new third storey
- before 1837, Barboros Radvilaitės g. 5A
- 1881, Didžioji g. 11: third storey on the SE wing
- 1889, Didžioji g. 14: third storey on the first wing
- early 20th c., Pilies g. 24: fourth storey
- late 20th c., Didžioji g. 35: fourth storey
Of the 232 listed buildings within 150 m, 177 have fabric dated to the 18th century or earlier (earliest century mentioned: 16th c. 67, 17th c. 42, 18th c. 44). A secondary source says tile roofs became mandatory for new houses after the mid-18th-century fires.

findings.claim: The Soviet-era architectural studies are offline, in VRVA fund 1019; one inventory is being digitised in 2026
findings.detail:
Studies and projects of the Paminklų restauravimo projektavimo institutas (PRPI) are in VRVA fund 1019: ap.11 scientific research files, ap.12 projects and measured drawings. The VRVA digitisation page lists 'Mokslinių-tiriamųjų darbų bylų apyrašas Nr. 11' for 2026, without saying how many files or where they will be published. Fund 1035 (aerial surveys and topographic plans, 1957–1989) is also being digitised; it is useful for roofs before the 1970s reconstructions.
The heritage department's library has about 19,000 printed items and 47 document collections of about 100,000 units: research reports, the 1978–87 monument register studies, and main dossiers. Addresses are Ašmenos g. 10 and Šnipiškių g. 3; no online catalogue of reports was found. Remote access means ordering copies by e-mail or phone.
KPEPIS (kpepis.lt), where research reports and restoration projects are filed, requires a login. The Old Town Renewal Agency (VSAA) mentions a new applied-research database but gives no public URL (contact Jurga Jackevičiūtė-Meškienė).

findings.claim: Several public-domain plans from c.1737 to 1805 can be georeferenced for footprint and plot checks
findings.detail:
Plans on Commons (per-file metadata):
- 'File:Vilnia, Staroje Miesta. Вільня, Старое Места (J. Kunicki, 1805).jpg': 8137x6230 px, source LVIA F.1135 ap.23 b.65 l.19, PD. The closest full Old Town plan to 1794.
- 'File:Vilnia. Вільня (1737) (Стары горад).jpg': Fürstenhoff plan, Staatsbibliothek zu Berlin, Kartensammlungen.
- 'File:Vilnia. Вільня (1800, 1912).jpg': 9951x8029 px, 'Wilno w końcu wieku XVIII.go', 1912 (Ruszczyc and Halicki), Biblioteka Narodowa ZZK 6 016; marked 'Domena Publiczna' on Polona.
- 'File:Vilnia. Вільня (1803).jpg': BnF GED-1803.
- 'File:Vilenskija zamki ... (1794, 1850-70).jpg': Lower and Upper Castle plan, MNW 145073/592.
- 'Ł. Gucevič, 1781-98': suburbs, Wróblewski Library F.229.
Other sources:
- 1808 city plan: in the heritage department's library (per the KVR act); not online.
- Russian military plans: 1793 and 1798 by F. Chomentovski, 1794, and 1799 by M. Markovich, in Russian State Military History Archive (RGVIA) fond 846. Russian archives are currently closed to Lithuanian researchers (secondary).
- Background: Čiurlionienė, 'Vilniaus miesto plano transformacijos XVIII a. pab.–XIX a.', Urbanistika ir architektūra 33(1) 2009, doi 10.3846/1392-1630.2009.33.11-19.

findings.claim: The key imagery for the spine is public domain: Smuglewicz 1785–86, Wilczyński's album, 19th–20th-century photographs and Polona postcards
findings.detail:
- Smuglewicz: Gate of Dawn view 1785–86, Biblioteka Narodowa F.40534/II (Commons, PD). Polona has 'fotografia akwareli Franciszka Smuglewicza' plates made before 1912 (Ostra Brama, walls, Lower Castle, gates), marked Domena Publiczna. The Kraków National Museum (MNK) holds 21 original watercolours (secondary).
- Commons: Album Wileńskie 201 files; Historical images of Pilies Street in Vilnius 108 files; Stanisław Filibert Fleury 116; Franciszek Smuglewicz 84; Old maps of Vilnius 134. The street categories (Pilies 137, Didžioji 151, Aušros Vartų 187 items) are mostly modern.
- Polona API (POST https://polona.pl/api/search-service/search/simple?query=...) returns many pre-1939 photos and postcards of 'ul. Zamkowa' (Pilies), 'ul. Wielka' (Didžioji), Ostra Brama and ratusz, most marked PD with commercial use allowed. Some 1930s items are reading-room only.
- Search under historical street names: Pilies = ul. Zamkowa / Замковая; Didžioji = ul. Wielka / Большая; Aušros Vartų = ul. Ostrobramska; the Soviet 'Gorkio g.' covered Pilies and Didžioji and appears in KVR citations.
- The Lithuanian National Museum of Art's 'Vilniaus gatvės' exhibitions (Pilies 2018, Didžioji 2019) have per-address pages and sociotopographic map PDFs. Example: the Town Hall page cites Gucevičius drawings of 1785–86 and a Januszewicz watercolour of the 1763 Town Hall.

findings.claim: epaveldas, LIMIS and the Vilnius University Library license item by item; none has a clear bulk API
findings.detail:
- epaveldas.lt (national library portal): each object carries a Creative Commons licence or Europeana RightsStatement; public-domain high-resolution files are marked PDM. Secondary summary.
- LIMIS (limis.lt): more than 112,000 public items from over 60 museums, feeding epaveldas and Europeana; licence and API details not found (info@limis.lt).
- VU Library digital collections (kolekcijos.biblioteka.vu.lt): graphics and photography collections; no licence or IIIF information on the 'Apie' page (skaitmenines.kolekcijos@mb.vu.lt). A previously cited object URL, VUB01_000679973, returned 404.
- LNDM (the national art museum) holds Bułhak, Czechowicz and Januszewicz material, accessible via LIMIS.
Pipeline rule: record rights per image, and treat anything without a PD or CC mark as reference-only.

findings.claim: Mapillary is CC BY-SA, but its API needs a token; spine coverage is unverified
findings.detail:
The Mapillary terms say other users' content 'is subject to the Creative Commons Share Alike (CC BY-SA) license, unless we indicate otherwise'. Section 12 limits commercial use to improving products or datasets and serving clients, and bans re-identification or unblurring. The Developer Tools need a registered client_id.
An unauthenticated call to graph.mapillary.com/images?bbox=... returned 'Invalid OAuth 2.0 Access Token' (code 190). The owner must create a free account and token, then query /images?bbox=25.284,54.673,25.292,54.687 with fields id, captured_at, is_pano, compass_angle to measure coverage. I did not create an account.

findings.claim: KartaView has effectively no imagery on the spine
findings.detail: The anonymous API 1.0 (POST https://api.openstreetcam.org/1.0/list/nearby-photos/, lat/lng/radius) returned 0 photos within 60 m of five spine points (Pilies, Didžioji, Town Hall, Aušros Vartų, Gate of Dawn). It also returned 0 within 300 m of Didžioji (54.6795, 25.2880). Within 1 km there are 215 photos from 2017, the nearest at 54.6857, 25.2859. KartaView imagery is CC BY-SA; the v2 read API needs authentication.

findings.claim: Google Street View, satellite, 45-degree and photorealistic 3D imagery cannot be used as a modelling reference
findings.detail:
- Google Maps/Earth Additional Terms (last modified 2026-01-27) prohibit: 'copy the content (unless ... permitted ... or applicable intellectual property law, including fair use)'; 'mass download'; creating mapping-related datasets for substitute services; and 'create a new product or service based on Google Maps'.
- Google's geo guidelines: 'You may not screenshot Street View imagery or remove it from embedded sources for any purpose.'
- Maps Platform EEA Terms 3.2.3(c), No Creating Content: no tracing of 'building outlines ... from Street View imagery' and no '3D building models from 45° Imagery'.
- Map Tiles API policies: overlaid 3D objects must not be 'extracted, traced, or otherwise derived by hand or machine from Photorealistic 3D Tiles'.
Viewing Street View in a browser for orientation is a legal grey zone under fair use or quotation. The pipeline should ban it as an evidence source.

findings.claim: Lithuanian state orthophotos, LiDAR and GRPK footprints are free under CC BY 4.0 with National Land Service attribution
findings.detail:
Environment Minister's order D1-395 of 2024-11-20 (in force 2025-01-01): data are free (point 5), reusable under CC BY 4.0 (point 21), attribution '[Logo] [Dataset name] © Nacionalinė žemės tarnyba prie Aplinkos ministerijos, [year]' (point 22).
Datasets:
- ORT2LT, 1:2000 county-centre ortho: pixel ≤10 cm, RMSE ≤0.2 m, 2017 flights. The data.gov.lt harvest describes the 2018 edition; a newer ORT2LT update is announced but its date is unverified.
- ORT10LT, national: 2025 flights of one third of the country, GSD ≤20 cm (25 cm in exceptions), RGB+NIR; 2024–26 three-year cycle.
- Lidar_DR, county centres, 2017: more than 30 (average 45) points/m2, RMSE horizontal <30 cm and vertical <10 cm, RGB-coloured .las.
- Lidar_DR_LT: 2025 (at least 15 points/m2, RIEGL, 2.3 TB) and 2026 releases; data.gov.lt dataset 3987 'Aktualiausi Lidar_DR_LT (2019–2026)'.
- 1944 orthophoto of Vilnius: geoportal service gisc_ort_1944.
- GRPK PASTAT footprint layer: already downloaded in the scratchpad.
- Lietuvos 3D žemėlapis (national 3D map): LOD1 buildings from GRPK plus LiDAR; FeatureServer tiiis_3d/PastataiLOD1FC, 166 models in the bbox with top altitude.

findings.claim: ID Vilnius serves oblique-derived reality meshes, very high-resolution orthophotos and a 3D buildings layer with height, storeys and year built; the licence is unverified
findings.detail:
Services referenced by the 3D Vilnius web scene (vplanas item cf8a21f5f8e0400db5e0a687da75f21a):
- opencity.idvilnius.lt/server/rest/services/3D/Vilnius_mesh_2019/SceneServer and Vilnius_mesh_2022/SceneServer: IntegratedMesh, 'reality mesh created with Bentley ContextCapture'
- Ortofoto/Orto_2022_WGS and Orto_2024_WGS: cache down to about 1.9 cm per pixel at the deepest level; source resolution unverified
- image/rest/services/BO/Vilnius_BO_ortofoto_aktualiausia: pixel 0.0072 m, probably drone patches
- Hosted/Pastatai_3D ('Esamos situacijos pastatai'): fields geom_height, geom_roof_min_h/max_h, Aukstai (storeys), STATMETAI (year built), NTRUNKNR (property number); attributes readable only through I3S statistics or nodes, with no FeatureServer
ID Vilnius also lists an oblique-photo product (idvilnius.lt 3D models page). No licence is stated. These are the best remote roof and facade references; ask ID Vilnius for written permission before relying on them.

findings.claim: Key printed and secondary works on house histories and plots (in copyright, reference only)
findings.detail:
- A. R. Čaplinskas, 'Vilniaus gatvių istorija. Valdovų kelias': Rūdninkų gatvė (2001), Didžioji gatvė (2002), Pilies gatvė (book 3, 2005). House-by-house histories.
- M. Klovas, E. Meilus, A. Urmański, O. Valionienė, 'Vilniaus sociotopografijos metmenys XIV–XVIII a.' (Lithuanian Institute of History, 2021): plot and owner history integrated in GIS.
- M. Paknys, 'Vilniaus miestas ir miestiečiai 1636 m.' (2006).
- K. Glinska and B. R. Vitkauskienė (eds), 'Atrastas Vilnius. Kartografiniai ir sociotopografiniai miesto maketo šaltiniai' (Lithuanian National Museum, 2023): first-third-of-19th-century plans and building drawings from RGVIA and the Russian naval archive (RGAVMF), used for the museum's 2023 model 'Vilnius prieš 200 metų' (dating given as c.1820s–1830s).
- V. Drėma, 'Dingęs Vilnius' (1991): iconography.
- J. Czechowicz, 'XIX amžiaus Vilniaus vaizdai' (1995).

findings.claim: How the AC Unity team rebuilt 1789 Paris
findings.detail:
- Ubisoft (news, 2024-11-01): a '1:1 re-creation of central Paris as it was in the 18th century'; earlier games built landmarks at about 4/5 scale for memory reasons.
- Historians: Laurent Turcot (Université du Québec à Trois-Rivières, daily life) and Jean-Clément Martin (Sorbonne, script review) per Wikipedia; in-house historian Maxime Durand.
- Designer Nicolas Guérin spent three months on more than 150 old plans (AFP via Malay Mail, 2014-07-27; Rodama blog 2015). No source found saying the Turgot plan specifically was used (unverified).
- Production manager Jeffery Spacer (2014-10-15): 38 major landmarks 'near one-to-one' with unique interiors; 'every one in five or six buildings' enterable.
- Notre-Dame (SIGGRAPH blog, 2019-05): Caroline Miousse used blueprints and historian input. They kept the modern (19th-century) spire for recognisability and climbability, and changed the interior 'to add several layers of navigation'. The 2 years / about 5,000 hours figure is secondary.
- A 'radial scale' (centre near 1:1, looser periphery) and art director Gambouz's 'Paris of the imagination' come only from search summaries (unverified).
Lessons for Vilnius: build landmarks 1:1; keep buildings' relative positions exact; any compression goes in a separate, flagged layer; add traversal affordances in period vocabulary; take anachronisms as explicit design decisions.

findings.claim: How heritage-visualisation projects back-date buildings: paradata, source transparency and per-feature uncertainty
findings.detail:
- London Charter, Principle 4 (Documentation): make clear whether a visualisation shows 'the existing state, an evidence-based restoration or an hypothetical reconstruction' and the extent of uncertainty; publish the full source list with provenance and the rationale for each decision (paradata).
- Seville Principles (ICOMOS; principles of virtual archaeology, adopted by the 2017 General Assembly per secondary sources): historical rigour, scientific transparency, and the distinctions between virtual restoration, reconstruction and recreation.
- Apollonio, Fallavollita and Foschi: a 7(+1)-level uncertainty scale applied per feature (geometry, constructive system, surface appearance, position) and shown in false colour. Urban-scale case study: Piazza delle Erbe, Verona (Heritage 2024, 7, 476–498, doi 10.3390/heritage7010023); an open Blender plugin exists.
- Local precedent: the Lithuanian National Museum's c.1820s–30s city model, built from military plans and building drawings.
For the game: A/B/C grades per feature, not per building.

findings.claim: Proposed repeatable per-building method (10 steps, remote only)
findings.detail:
1. Footprint seed: GRPK polygon (TOP_ID) as the master geometry, cross-walked to OSM ids and the address; add ID Vilnius NTRUNKNR where possible.
2. KVR join: spatial and address join against pub_kvr_objektai layers 0/1, giving code and GUID(s) and the parent complex.
3. Harvest from KVR: Century, Style, Author, ObjectFeatures, documents and attachments, photo list. Parse dated alteration notes into events (storey added, facade remodelled, balcony, shopfront, window change, roof change).
4. Read the acts: history narrative, 1790s owner, and archive call numbers. Queue remote scan orders (VRVA f.1019 PRPI studies and 1960s–70s measured drawings; LVIA; the heritage department's main dossiers; 1808 plan).
5. Georeference Kunicki 1805, Fürstenhoff 1737, the 1912 'late-18th-c.' plan and the 1944 ortho. Confirm the footprint existed in 1794 and the plot boundaries (plot data from Klovas et al. 2021).
6. Iconography sweep with historical street names on Commons, Polona, epaveldas/LIMIS and the national art museum's street pages. Log each image's date, view direction, holder, call number and rights.
7. Modern metrics from LiDAR: eave and ridge heights, roof planes, storey rows. Cross-check with Pastatai_3D, the ORT2LT/ID Vilnius orthos and the meshes (if licensed); Mapillary only if it has coverage.
8. Back-dating operations, each tied to evidence IDs: e.g. remove the post-1794 storey, restore steep tile roof, remove shopfront or balcony, restore window axes.
9. Grade every feature A/B/C and record paradata.
10. Separate gameplay layer (handholds, rooftop links, opened gateways, scale tweaks), each item flagged as a deviation. Historian review, then lock the dossier.

findings.claim: Proposed building registry data model
findings.detail:
One record per modelled building. Fields:
- building_id
- geometry: grpk_top_id, osm_ids[], footprint_source (GRPK|OSM|KVR-TRP|plan-1805|manual), footprint_1794_status (same|extended|merged|new-after-1794) with evidence_ids, plot_ref_1805, courtyard_ids[]
- address: current, historical names (PL, RU, Soviet), owner_1790s with source
- heritage: kvr_codes[], kvr_guids[], kvr_status, parent_complex_code, in_site_16073 (bool), kvr_century_text, kvr_style, kvr_authors[]
- modern: eave_h_m, ridge_h_m, height_source (Lidar_DR-2017 tile or Lidar_DR_LT-2025), storeys_now, roof_form_now, roof_material_now, year_built_registry (STATMETAI)
- state_1794: exists (Y/N/partial), storeys, eave_h_m, ridge_h_m, roof_form, roof_pitch_deg, roof_material, facade_style, window_axes, ground_floor_use, gateway/passage (įvaža), galleries, facade_colour
- alteration_history[]: date_from, date_to, precision, type, description, evidence_ids, grade
- backdating_ops[]: op, params, evidence_ids, grade
- evidence[]: id, type (register-text|act-pdf|photo|drawing|plan|lidar|ortho|mesh|book|archive-scan), title, creator, date or range, depicts_date, holder, call_number, url, licence (SPDX or RightsStatement), use (reference|redistributable), view_direction, notes
- confidence per feature: massing, height, roof, facade, openings, details, colour. A = documented (dated evidence up to c.1800, or an explicitly dated post-1794 alteration, or a study-verified surviving fabric). B = inferred (1805–1870s evidence plus typology, or undated 19th-c. alteration). C = conjectural (typology only). Map to Apollonio levels.
- gameplay: climbable_faces, ledge/handhold density, rooftop_route_segments[], courtyard_gateway (open/closed/added), interior (none/partial/full), scale_deviation, anachronism_flags[] with justification
- workflow: status, reviewer, updated, paradata_note

findings.claim: Rules for estimating 1794 heights when evidence is missing (proposal; numbers to be calibrated)
findings.detail:
R1. Measure the modern eave and ridge from LiDAR (Lidar_DR 2017, checked against the 2025–26 scans). Count storeys from facade window rows in KVR photos.
R2. Use any dated storey event in KVR or the acts: before 1794 keep the storey (e.g. Pilies 17, 1718); after 1794 remove it (e.g. Pilies 8, 1800). Grade A.
R3. Clues to a later top storey: a 'late 19th-c. / historicist' remodel on a 16th–17th-c. core; a top floor with different window rhythm or height; KVR phrases such as 'karnizas tarnauja kaip tarpaukštinė trauka' (the old eaves cornice now reads as a string course, e.g. Arklių g. 10). Then storeys_1794 = storeys_now - 1 (grade B).
R4. Default for main-street houses without clues: 2 storeys plus cellar and a steep tiled roof, 3 if the house is a palace or large corner house (grade C). Courtyard wings: 1–2 storeys, since the register often dates wing raising to the 19th c.
R5. Removed-storey height: the measured top floor-to-floor height, or else the median of A-graded neighbours on the same street (calibrate on the roughly 30 buildings with dated events).
R6. Roofs: steep gable or hip with ceramic tiles as the 1794 default (the post-fire tile rule is secondary-sourced; the pitch value is unverified). Ridge orientation and attics are taken from the 1805 plan, Smuglewicz, Wilczyński and early photos.
R7. Churches, monasteries, palaces, the Town Hall and the Gate of Dawn are always modelled from evidence, never from typology.
R8. Do not level the eaves line; the street was historically uneven.

findings.claim: Ship game geometry derived from GRPK (CC BY 4.0), not OSM (ODbL share-alike)
findings.detail: OSM data is under ODbL (as the Overpass response header states). A derivative database of footprints distributed with the game could trigger share-alike obligations. GRPK and the other state datasets require attribution only (order D1-395, CC BY 4.0). OSM is still useful for addresses, names and tags during research. GRPK footprint counts match OSM within about 5–10% in every band.

risks: The KVR JSON API is undocumented: it can change without notice (a KVR and KPEPIS consolidation project is under way) and its search endpoints reject scripted calls. Cache everything locally (already harvested to the scratchpad) and keep request rates low.

Rights for KVR photos, acts' appendices, ID Vilnius meshes and orthophotos, LIMIS and VU Library images are not stated. Treat them as reference-only until KPD and ID Vilnius confirm in writing; never redistribute or texture directly from them.

KVR 'valuable features' describe today's protected fabric, not the 1794 state. Older registrations (2003–2005) are thin, and iconography appendices are often offline, so some A grades will need paid archive scans.
Storey additions range from 1718 to the late 20th century. A blanket rule of 2 storeys in 1794 would wrongly shorten some buildings (e.g. Pilies 17, Dominikonų 15) and leave others too tall.

KVR objects do not map one-to-one to footprints: complexes, parts and multi-wing houses exist, and polygon centroids are territories, not buildings. Hand-check the joins for the roughly 100 frontage buildings.
Using Google Street View, Earth or 3D Tiles would breach Google's terms (screenshots, tracing and derived 3D models are all prohibited). Enforce this as a team rule.

Mapillary coverage is unknown and KartaView is empty. With field capture ruled out, facade texture detail depends on KVR photos (permission needed), Polona and Commons photos (PD but old and monochrome) and meshes (licence unknown).
Russian archives (RGVIA fond 846, the 1790s plans) are closed. The 'Atrastas Vilnius' publication is the only practical route to that material.
Shipping OSM-derived footprints could trigger ODbL share-alike; use GRPK.

The 1794 construction-site states of the Town Hall (Gucevičius rebuild 1786–1799) and the Cathedral force the same kind of recognisability-vs-accuracy anachronism decision that Ubisoft made for Notre-Dame.
open_questions: Does 'remote only' allow paid scan orders from archives (VRVA fund 1019, LVIA, the heritage department's library dossiers and 1808 plan), or only material already online?
Will the owner create a Mapillary account and token so spine coverage can be measured, and accept CC BY-SA imagery as a reference?
Will ID Vilnius grant permission to use the 2019/2022 reality meshes, the 2024 and drone orthophotos and the Pastatai_3D attributes as modelling references? Contact via idvilnius.lt.

Does 'Atrastas Vilnius' (Lithuanian National Museum, 2023) reproduce facade drawings of every Pilies, Didžioji and Aušros Vartų house? If so, buying the book would lift many buildings from grade C to B.
Target date policy: strictly 1794, or c.1794 ±10 years for ambiguous events (e.g. Didžioji g. 15, third storey added in the late 18th or early 19th century)?
Scale policy: strict 1:1 for the whole spine, or Unity-style compression outside the frontage band? How will deviations be shown to players?
How should buildings mid-reconstruction in 1794 appear: the Town Hall, the Cathedral, and ruins such as the Lower Castle palace?
Are there Old Town facade polychromy studies (VSAA or PRPI colour projects, e.g. VRVA f.1019 ap.12 b.32982 for Pilies 19) that could set 1794 colours, or will colour stay grade C?

checks.claim: KVR bulk open data: data.gov.lt dataset 2192, CC BY 4.0, updated quarterly, last updated 2025-12-18, 26,059 immovable rows, no addresses or coordinates; coordinates request 14527 filed 2026-09-19
checks.correction: Confirmed: the licence (CC BY 4.0), the 'quarterly' label, the 2025-12-18 metadata update, publisher KPD, request 14527 (2026-09-19 12:15) and the absence of address, dating and coordinates. Corrected: both XLSX distributions are listed as published and updated 2023-02-01. The latest registracijos_data in the immovable file is Excel serial 44957 (2023-01-31), so the file is a January 2023 snapshot and is not refreshed quarterly. 26,059 is the line count including the header, so there are 26,058 objects. The file also has statuso_keitimo_data and tipas columns. Use the live ArcGIS or JSON service for current status, not the XLSX.

checks.claim: KVR public ArcGIS REST service pub_kvr_objektai (ArcGIS 10.3): layer 0 points, layer 1 polygons; fields ObjectId, Code, Name, NameOfficial, ObjectName, Status, Address; maxRecordCount 1000; bbox gives 244 points + 226 polygons = 470
checks.correction: Service, version 10.3, fields, maxRecordCount 1000 and native SR (wkid 2600 / latestWkid 3346) all confirmed. copyrightText is empty, so no licence is stated. My intersects count for the same bbox (25.284–25.292 E, 54.673–54.687 N) was 248 points + 226 polygons = 474, against the report's 470. The small difference is probably method (intersects vs within), not a factual error. Other services listed: kvr_apsaugos_zonos, kvr_objektai_centras, kvr_objektai, kvr_paieska, kvr_teritoriju_ribos, pub_kvr_apsaugos_zonos, pub_kvr_paieska.

checks.claim: Undocumented KVR JSON service (LabbisServiceKvr.svc/GetStaticHeritageDetails) gives dated alteration chronology. Examples: Pilies g. 19 (27443) 'pastatytas XVI a.; Š flygelis XIX a. I p., rekonstruotas XIX a. pab., XX a. pr., 1974 m.', architect V. Gorskis; Pilies g. 17 third storey 1718; Pilies g. 8 third storey 1800
checks.correction:
Live calls on 2026-09-26 confirm the texts:
- 27443 (GUID 8862d9ad…): the Century text above; Author 'rekonstrukcijos autorius Vincentas Gorskis (1848 - po 1901 m.)'; features '3 a. su rūsiais', 'dvišlaitė'.
- 27440 Pilies 17: 'pastatytas XVI a., 1718 m. rekonstruotas, užstatytas III a.; 1889-1893 m. rekonstruotas'.
- 650 Pilies 8 / Bernardinų 1: 'statytas XVII a. pr., po 1758 m. gaisro atstatytas, 1800 m. užstatytas trečias aukštas, remontuotas 1828 m., rekonstruotas 1863 m.…'.
Caveat: Pilies 8 is an irregular U-plan of 2–3-storey wings, and the register does not say which wing was raised in 1800. '2 storeys in 1794, grade A' holds only for the wing(s) the act identifies. Note also a 1758 fire rebuild the report omits.

checks.claim: Act KPD-RM-1586/1 (2024-11-05) for Pilies g. 19 is a 12-page PDF with font encoding shifted by 29; it names the 1790 owner Karl Friedrich Trebert of Königsberg
checks.correction: Downloaded attachment E48E8B62-…: 12 pages, 'AKTAS 2024-11-05 Nr. KPD-RM-1586/1'. After a +29 code-point shift the text reads '1790 m. priklausė iš Karaliaučiaus kilusiam bajorui Karoliui Frydrichui Trebertui (Trebert)'. In the early 19th c. the owner was Jacques Antoine Briotet, anatomy professor at Vilnius University. The report missed that the same act gives period ground-floor use: shops, storage, a distillery and a stable with shed, with the 2nd floor residential. This is direct evidence for the ground_floor_use field.

checks.claim: Town Hall: Gucevičius rebuild 1786–1799, so it was a construction site in 1794
checks.correction: The Visuotinė lietuvių enciklopedija (VLE): the leaning tower collapsed in 1781 while Gucevičius was strengthening its foundations, and the Town Hall was rebuilt '1785–99' to his design on the old foundations and cellars, with shops attached. The Town Hall's own history page: projects prepared in 1786, construction began in 1788, finished in 1799. The honest range is 1785/1788–1799, not 1786–1799. The construction-site conclusion stands and matters for the story: Hetman Szymon Kossakowski was hanged in Town Hall Square on 25 April 1794, in front of this unfinished building.

checks.claim: The 1808 city plan is only in the heritage department's library and is not online
checks.correction: A georeferenced 1808 topography is online. The city portal 'Vilniaus DNR' (Vilniaus planas / ID Vilnius, opened 2023-03-01 for Vilnius's 700th anniversary) publishes a '1808 m. plano rekonstrukcija' at https://zemelapiai.vplanas.lt/vilniausdnr/lt/periods/compare/timeline/1808. The raster layer is 'VilniausDNR_T1808', subject '1808 m. topografija (rastras)', LKS-94, tiled down to 1:500. Tile export is disabled, the REST folder needs a token, and no licence is stated, so treat it as view-only. The Lithuanian Institute of History's plot-history review also says the 1808 plan is the base for reconstructing Old Town plots because it marks plot boundaries. This largely removes the need to order the 1808 plan as a scan for plot checks.

checks.claim: Jan Kunicki's 1805 Old Town plan on Commons: 8137x6230 px, LVIA F.1135 ap.23 b.65 l.19, public domain; the closest full Old Town plan to 1794
checks.correction:
Commons metadata confirmed: 8,137 × 6,230 px, Jan Kunicki, 1805, LVIA F.1135 ap.23 b.65 l.19, Public Domain Mark. The LVIA call number itself was not checked against the archive's catalogue. Qualifier: Commons also has period plans the report under-uses:
- a plan of the Upper and Lower Castles dated 1794 (a copy made 1850–70; MNW 145073/592; 2932×2193). It is the key source for the Cathedral/Lower Castle end of the spine.
- Vilnius University Library plans from 1799–1800, e.g. the Bernardine monastery, 1799, 7115×5638.

checks.claim: 'Wilno w końcu wieku XVIII.go' (1912, Ruszczyc and Halicki, BN ZZK 6 016) is a 1912 reprint of a late-18th-century plan
checks.correction: Polona record b0000003694570: 'Wilno w końcu wieku XVIII.go', Wilno: nakł. J. Zawadzkiego, 1912. It is one two-colour map, 27.5 × 36.0 cm. Contributors are 'Ruszczyc, Ferdynand (1870-1936). Rys.', 'Halicki, A. Rys.' and 'Smuglewicz, Franciszek'. Call number ZZK 6 016, Domena Publiczna (commercial use allowed). The Commons scan is 9951×8029. 'Rys.' (drawn by) and the small format point to a newly drawn 1912 illustrative reconstruction, not a facsimile of an 18th-c. survey. What 18th-c. source it follows is unverified. Use it as secondary evidence only, not for plot geometry.

checks.claim: The 1737 Fürstenhoff plan (Staatsbibliothek zu Berlin) can be georeferenced for footprint and plot checks
checks.correction: Author (Johann Georg Maximilian von Fürstenhoff), date 1737 and holder (Staatsbibliothek zu Berlin, Kartensammlungen) are confirmed on Commons. But the Commons files are only 718×800 px (central crop) and 2,048×1,454 px (full plan, credited to 'Vilniaus Vaizdų Archyvas'). That is too coarse to check plots. Georeferencing needs a high-resolution scan from the Staatsbibliothek; the shelfmark is unverified. It also predates the 1748 and 1749 fires, so it shows the street network, not the 1794 buildings.

checks.claim: Smuglewicz's Gate of Dawn view, 1785–86, Biblioteka Narodowa F.40534/II, public domain on Commons; National Museum in Kraków holds 21 original watercolours
checks.correction: Commons file 'Vilnia, Vostraja Brama… (F. Smuglevič, 1785-86).jpg': 3893×2501, credit 'Biblioteka Narodowa. F.40534/II.', PD. The 21 Kraków originals plus copies by Józef Peszka rest on a secondary source (Magazyn Wileński 2007). Planning note: this view shows the pre-1829 Baroque chapel. VLE: the wooden chapel of 1671 burned in 1715 and a Baroque brick chapel replaced it; the present Classicist chapel front dates from 1829 and the gallery from 1830. Today's Gate of Dawn chapel cannot be 'back-dated' by subtraction.

checks.claim: A secondary source (ldkistorija) says tile roofs became mandatory for new houses after the mid-18th-century fires
checks.correction: The cited page lists city fire-prevention measures without dating them: brick houses and tile roofs within the walls, fire trades moved outside the walls, chimney rules, curfews. It does not tie tile roofs to the period after 1737/1748/1749, and it does not say 'new houses'. The fire dates it does give: 2 June 1737, 11 June 1748, 8 June 1749. Keep 'steep tile roof' as a typological default graded C, not a sourced rule. Pilies g. 8's register entry does list 'molio čerpių' (clay tile) roofing today.

checks.claim: Order D1-395 (2024-11-20, in force 2025-01-01) makes state orthophotos, LiDAR and GRPK free under CC BY 4.0 with National Land Service attribution (points 5, 21, 22)
checks.correction: Text confirmed. Point 2 of the order: in force 2025-01-01. Point 5: data 'teikiami neatlygintinai' (free of charge). Point 21: 'Creative Commons BY 4.0'. Point 22: attribution form '[Logotipas] [Duomenų pavadinimas] © Nacionalinė žemės tarnyba prie Aplinkos ministerijos, [metai]'. The report missed two points. First, the order covers only datasets on the list approved by order D1-261 (2023-08-01). Second, point 9: a geoportal order must be confirmed through the state interoperability identity platform (Lithuanian e-ID) or with a qualified e-signature. Point 12: bulk ORT2LT/Lidar_DR/Lidar_DR_LT deliveries need a request signed with a qualified e-signature. A team without Lithuanian e-ID or an eIDAS qualified signature will need a local partner.

checks.claim: Russian military plans of Vilnius (1793 and 1798 by F. Chomentovski, 1794, 1799 by M. Markovich) are in RGVIA fond 846; Russian archives are closed to Lithuanian researchers
checks.correction: RGVIA fond 846 is plausible: it is the Military-Scientific Archive (VUA) collection, which holds topographic and cartographic material. No source found names the specific plans or authors. They are not in the cited Čiurlionienė 2009 article; its correct DOI is 10.3846/13921630.2009.33.11-19, and the hyphenated form redirects there. The access closure is also unverified. There is a partial online route the report missed: the Presidential Library (prlib.ru) hosts digitised Russian-archive plans of Vilna, e.g. item 324292, an 1818 plan of the 'Mощи Иисуса' foundling home. Weigh the licensing and sanctions issues before using it.

OTHER CLAIMS CONFIRMED (not in the list above):
- Google geo guidelines say "You may not screenshot Street View imagery or remove it from embedded sources for any purpose." They also ban tracing or digitising Street View and using Google Earth output to rebuild 3D models.
- Mapillary: other users' content is CC BY-SA, and commercial use is limited (terms effective 2024-02-15).
- Ubisoft's news post of 2024-11-01 says "1:1 re-creation of central Paris as it was in the 18th century"; earlier games built landmarks at about 4/5 scale.
- Unity historians Turcot and Martin are named on Wikipedia. The SIGGRAPH post confirms Caroline Miousse and Maxime Durand, and that the team kept the modern spire. It gives no 2-year / 5,000-hour figure.
- The Seville Principles were ratified by the 19th ICOMOS General Assembly, New Delhi, December 2017.
- Apollonio, Fallavollita, Foschi and Smurra, Heritage 7(1):476–498, published 2024-01-19, doi 10.3390/heritage7010023. The report left out Smurra as a co-author.
- VRVA fund 1019 holds the Monument Restoration Design Institute (PRPI) records, 1949–1993. The archive's page (updated 2026-05-08) says digitisation of inventory 11 'continues' in 2026, so it started earlier. Fund 1035 aerial surveys are listed as 1957, 1961–68, 1963, 1975 and 1976–89.
- Čaplinskas volumes: Rūdninkų 2001, Didžioji 2002, Pilies 2005. There is no volume for Aušros Vartų g., which is a gap for that street.
- Klovas et al. 2021: Lithuanian Institute of History, 334 pp., ISBN 9786098314069. A copy is on Academia.edu.
- The Lithuanian National Museum model 'Vilnius prieš 200 metų' was presented on 2023-05-11, led by Birutė Vitkauskienė. The LRT article does not name the Russian military (RGVIA) or naval (RGAVMF) archives as sources, so that detail is unverified.
- Cathedral: rebuilding began in 1783 to Gucevičius's 1781 design and was finished in 1801 by M. Šulcas.

WHAT THE REPORT GOT ANACHRONISTIC OR MISSED. The 'today's building, back-dated' method cannot produce these:
1. City walls and gates stood in 1794. Most of the wall and all gates except the Gate of Dawn were torn down in 1799–1805. The Aušros Vartų end of the spine was a working fortified gate in a standing wall.
2. The Lower Castle and the Palace of the Grand Dukes were razed in 1801. Today's palace is a 21st-century reconstruction and must not be back-dated. The open Cathedral Square did not exist in its present form: in 1794 this end of the spine was the castle precinct, the Cathedral under reconstruction, and palace ruins.
3. Gate of Dawn chapel: in 1794 it was the Baroque chapel built after 1715. Its present Classicist front dates from 1829 and the gallery from 1830.
4. Didžioji St.:
- St Nicholas Orthodox church (Didžioji 12) got its Byzantine look in 1845, with a chapel added in 1865.
- Pyatnitskaya church (Didžioji 2) was rebuilt in 1864.
- Chodkiewicz palace (Didžioji 4) was rebuilt in Classicist style after its 1803 sale. The exact dates vary between sources; unverified.
- The Town Hall had shops attached to it.
5. Aušros Vartų g. 5, the Philharmonic, was built 1899–1902 (architect K. Korojedovas). It did not exist in 1794.
6. The Presidential Palace was then the Bishops' Palace (burned in 1748). It was rebuilt in 1824–34 by V. Stasov.
7. St Casimir's crown dome dates from 1749–55 (Žebrauskas). The church was given to the Orthodox in 1841 and the crown was restored in 1942–43. Today's look is close to 1794, but that closeness comes from a restoration, not continuity.
8. Event anchors for the story:
- Vilnius uprising on the night of 22/23 April 1794, led by Jakub Jasiński.
- Szymon Kossakowski hanged in Town Hall Square on 25 April 1794.
- The city capitulated to Knorring on 12 August 1794.
- Čiurlionienė 2009 notes that Gucevičius, the architect of both the Cathedral and the Town Hall then under construction, took an active part in the 1794 uprising.
9. The Vilniaus DNR portal also carries 1845, 1911, 1938 and 1977 georeferenced plans and a Wróblewski Library historical-maps service. Licences are unverified.
10. The Lithuanian Institute of History's review of Old Town plot development (16th–18th c.) is openly online and uses the 1808 plan as its base.
